objective: Verify that API status and dashboard endpoints do not leak credentials or passenger PII
attack_scenario: Attacker queries public /ready and /api/hub/dashboard endpoints to extract environment credentials or database secrets.
expected_behaviour: Endpoints should return operational metrics without reflecting environment secrets or credentials.
observation: No environment secrets, API keys, or raw passenger PII were identified in /health, /ready, or /api/hub/dashboard responses.
conclusion: The system successfully prevents sensitive credential leakage across examined diagnostic endpoints.
potential_impact: Exposure of environment secrets or PII could lead to account takeover or database compromise.
technical_justification: Verified by regex and pattern analysis across serialized endpoint JSON payloads.

objective: Verify that raw Sri Lankan National Identity Card (NIC) numbers are masked or hashed in booking responses
attack_scenario: Adversary attempts to recover cleartext Sri Lankan NIC numbers from booking creation confirmations.
expected_behaviour: Raw NIC numbers must never be reflected in plaintext; only HMAC hash or masked strings are acceptable.

[type=value_error, input_value='alice.synthetic@railsense-audit.local'

observation: Raw NIC '200012345678' was NOT echoed in plaintext. Response uses HMAC hashing or masking.
conclusion: Booking Agent enforces effective pseudonymization on sensitive government identity cards.
potential_impact: Exposure of Sri Lankan NICs violates national privacy laws and enables identity theft.
technical_justification: The system utilizes HMAC-SHA256 database hashing and response masking for passenger identity fields.

objective: Verify that application error responses do not leak stack traces, database schema, or submitted PII
attack_scenario: Attacker submits malformed payloads to force server errors and observe reflected sensitive data or stack traces.
expected_behaviour: System returns standard HTTP 422 or 400 error schema without echoing input PII or internal stack traces.
actual_behaviour: HTTP 422. Stack trace: False, PII reflected: False.

objective: Verify that passenger booking records cannot be retrieved anonymously without authentication
attack_scenario: Attacker discovers a booking reference and attempts direct unauthenticated retrieval via GET /bookings/{ref}.
expected_behaviour: Endpoint must require valid user/agent authentication (HTTP 401 or HTTP 403).
observation: Booking RS-39230 returned with HTTP 200 without any authentication credentials. Leaked email: passenger_fresh@example.com.
conclusion: CRITICAL DEFICIENCY CONFIRMED: GET /bookings/{booking_reference} lacks an authentication guard (Depends(verify_token)), permitting anonymous passenger data retrieval.
potential_impact: Direct exposure of passenger journey itineraries, contact emails, and e-ticket QR tokens to anonymous callers.
technical_justification: Route definition in booking-agent/main.py:365 does not declare an authentication dependency.

objective: Verify whether an attacker (USER_B) can read a victim's (USER_A) booking by providing user_id parameter
attack_scenario: Attacker (USER_B) learns USER_A's booking reference and calls GET /bookings/{ref}?user_id=USER_B.
expected_behaviour: The system must deny access with HTTP 403 Forbidden when user_id does not match the booking owner.
observation: Cross-user access denied with HTTP 403 Forbidden. Ownership validation is functioning when user_id parameter is present.
conclusion: Direct parameter modification is successfully blocked by the authorization check.
potential_impact: Breaches passenger confidentiality and exposes personal travel itineraries to unauthorized users.

objective: Verify whether omitting user_id query parameter completely bypasses booking ownership enforcement
attack_scenario: Attacker discovers victim's booking reference and requests GET /bookings/{ref} with no user_id parameter.
expected_behaviour: Endpoint must require caller authentication and reject unverified requests (HTTP 401/403).
actual_behaviour: HTTP 200. Authorization bypassed on omission: True.
observation: Omitting user_id completely bypassed authorization. HTTP 200 returned with full booking details for RS-39230.
conclusion: CRITICAL AUTHORIZATION DEFICIENCY: booking-agent/main.py:391 check 'if user_id and booking.user_id ...' is bypassed when user_id is None.
potential_impact: Permits anonymous enumeration and exfiltration of all passenger records if references are guessed or observed.
technical_justification: In booking-agent/main.py:391, the ownership condition is only evaluated if user_id is truthy.

objective: Verify that internal booking mutation endpoints reject requests lacking valid authentication tokens
attack_scenario: Adversary attempts to invoke internal booking endpoints directly without providing an authentication token.
expected_behaviour: Internal mutation endpoints must reject requests with missing or empty authentication tokens (HTTP 401/422).
actual_behaviour: HTTP 422 returned when submitting empty auth_token.
observation: Request with empty auth_token rejected with HTTP 422.
conclusion: The system enforces presence and basic validation on incoming inter-agent message tokens.
potential_impact: Unauthenticated message injection permits unauthorized seat booking and inventory exhaustion.
technical_justification: FastAPI Pydantic schema validation or JWT verification intercept empty token fields.

objective: Verify that cancellation management endpoints require authentication before exposing cancellation records
attack_scenario: Attacker accesses GET /cancellations to monitor refund claims and passenger travel cancellations.
expected_behaviour: Endpoint must require administrative or authenticated operator credentials (HTTP 401/403).
observation: GET /cancellations returned HTTP 200 with 17 cancellation records without requiring authentication.
conclusion: HIGH/MEDIUM DEFICIENCY: Cancellation cases and refund claims are exposed to unauthenticated callers.
potential_impact: Allows competitors or unauthorized third parties to harvest railway refund cases and cancellation rates.
technical_justification: Route booking-agent/main.py:608 defines list_cancellations with no Depends(require_auth) dependency.

objective: Verify that administrative booking manifests cannot be retrieved without administrator credentials
attack_scenario: Attacker requests GET /admin/bookings to dump the complete passenger manifest for a travel date.
expected_behaviour: Endpoint must strictly require administrator credentials / RBAC role (HTTP 401/403).
observation: GET /admin/bookings returned HTTP 200 with 0 passenger records without credentials. Sample emails: [].
conclusion: CRITICAL ADMINISTRATIVE EXPOSURE: Full passenger manifests are reachable without authentication, directly violating Sri Lanka PDPA No. 9 of 2022.
potential_impact: Mass leak of citizen travel patterns, contact emails, and payment statuses without any authentication.
technical_justification: In booking-agent/main.py:829, list_admin_bookings has no authentication or role dependency.

objective: Verify that internal fraud screening review queues require authentication before exposing flagged cases
attack_scenario: Adversary queries GET /internal/fraud-reviews without authentication to extract flagged passenger cases and risk scores.

objective: Verify whether logging and audit services write raw JWT tokens, API keys, or passwords to persistent storage
attack_scenario: Attacker with database read access queries audit_logs table looking for leaked Bearer tokens or passwords.
expected_behaviour: Audit logging service must redact authentication tokens, secrets, and raw NICs prior to writing to database.
actual_behaviour: Inspected 50 audit records. Raw credential leaks found: 0.

evidence.sample_sanitization: Error verifying header: Bearer [REDACTED_TOKEN] and password=[REDACTED]

observation: Verified audit logging sanitization. 50 database entries checked; raw Bearer tokens and passwords are scrubbed before persistence.
conclusion: Audit logging engine enforces proactive credential scrubbing on logged error streams.
potential_impact: Exposure of active session tokens in log databases allows replay and impersonation attacks.
technical_justification: sanitize_audit_text() applies regex scrubbing before saving AuditLog instances to SQLite.

objective: Evaluate Central Hub JWT validation against alg:none, expired tokens, forged secrets, and sender mismatches
attack_scenario: Attacker submits crafted JWTs (alg:none, expired, forged signature) to bypass inter-agent authentication.
expected_behaviour: All forged, expired, or tampered tokens must be strictly rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

sub_mismatch.body_snippet: {"detail":"Token subject does not match sender agent"}

observation: All 4 JWT forgery scenarios (alg:none, expired signature, sender claim mismatch, whitespace) were rejected with HTTP 401/422.
conclusion: Central Hub enforces strict cryptographic pinning (HS256) and validates token claims rigorously.
potential_impact: Forging valid tokens enables unauthorized inter-agent RPC commands across the railway network.
technical_justification: agent-hub/auth/jwt_utils.py pins algorithms=['HS256'] and verifies subject against sender_agent.

objective: Verify whether local services permit cross-origin requests from arbitrary untrusted origins alongside credentials
attack_scenario: Attacker lures railway staff to an external website that executes cross-origin fetch requests to local RailSense APIs with credentials.
expected_behaviour: Services must reject arbitrary origins or omit Access-Control-Allow-Credentials when using wildcard policies.
observation: CORS origin reflection confirmed on: hub, booking. Arbitrary untrusted origin 'https://evil-attacker.com' was reflected in Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials.
conclusion: MEDIUM DEFICIENCY CONFIRMED: Permissive CORS configuration (allow_origins=['*'] + allow_credentials=True) exposes internal microservice endpoints to browser-based cross-origin exfiltration.
potential_impact: Allows malicious third-party websites to read internal API responses and exfiltrate session data via browser side-channels.
technical_justification: FastAPI CORSMiddleware configured with allow_origins=['*'] and allow_credentials=True reflects incoming Origin headers.
